title: NEW L2-only — every run dies deterministically at the Interview→Offer seam: the screen step double-advances the survivor (accept + screening_review accept), so the interview step's closing advanceTo('Offer') bare-accepts an Offer-stage entry to Hired and throws — phases 6–7 and the conversion CTA never play
expected: Journey DoD: a keyless end-to-end JD→Hired run whose offer step truly opens /offer/[token] and clicks Accept, finishing on the 'do it with your roles' CTA.
got: Live: entry 200 keyless, phases Design/Source/Intake/Screen/Interview traverse real tabs in 42s — then the bar turns red: 'Failed: Could not advance entry m-cand-007-jd-dhbye8rf to "Offer" within 4 steps (stalled at "Hired").' done:false and getStartedHref:null after the driver waited a further ~7 minutes; the stepper stays on '5 Interview' and the button reverts to 'Start simulation'. Mechanism (deterministic, code-traced): (1) the screen step advances the survivor Screened→Interview (SimulationProvider.tsx:493), THEN attaches the screening draft (:494 — sim/screen-draft sets screening_review regardless of stage, route.ts:24), THEN accepts it (:495); accepting a screening_review ADVANCES A STAGE and sets a calendar gate with default slot 'Tue 14:00' (app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1322-1331) — the survivor lands at OFFER, one stage past where the engine believes it is. (2) The interview step schedules a candidate already at Offer (approve_event tolerates it without regressing stage, pipeline.ts:1304-1309) and closes with advanceTo(targetId,'Offer') (:547). (3) advanceTo's first bare accept advances Offer→Hired via the generic path (pipeline.ts:1332-1340 — no offer_review, so the extend-offer gate is skipped), the remaining accepts no-op at terminal Hired, the loop never observes 'Offer', and it throws (SimulationProvider.tsx:268). Live artifacts match the trace exactly: activity shows 'advanced to Offer' BEFORE the schedule events and 'advanced to Hired' after; the calendar shows SIM Vít Malý at pipeline.ts:1330's hardcoded 'Tue 14:00'; the board says '1 candidate hired this week'.
evidence: shots/l2-helena-21-sim-pipeline.aria.txt:387-398 (activity: advanced to Interview → advanced to Offer → schedule events → advanced to Hired, all today)
shots/l2-helena-20-sim-done.aria.txt:127-135 ('Vít Malý, Experienced, Senior Java Backend Engineer (SIM)' at Tue 14:00 — the screening_review branch's default slot)
app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:1332-1340 (generic accept: Offer→Hired, no offer gate)
scope_note: Adversarially checked: not residue (entry id ties to this run's fresh JD jd-dhbye8rf; seals timestamped 14:22 today), not latency (thrown, not timed out), not a race (the double-advance is unconditional). Petra's step-mode/About entry runs the identical run() engine — step mode only gates between steps — so her stakeholder show dies at the same seam. SURFACE-MODEL GAP for the harness: L1 verified each endpoint in isolation but never composed the stage arithmetic across screen-draft → screening_review-accept → advanceTo; journey-level stage bookkeeping needs to join the L1 checklist.
l2_priority: recertify: run /api/demo auto-play to completion — phases 6 and 7 must highlight, the offer iframe must open /offer/[token] and click Accept, and the done state must render the CTA. Then run the About-tab step-mode entry to the same end.
suggested_acceptance: The screen step attaches the draft while the entry is still Screened (or the sim accepts via a non-advancing review action); advanceTo treats an entry already past the target as the labelled failure it is WITHOUT first mutating it; a sim e2e test pins JD→Hired completing with done:true and the CTA rendered.

title: NEW L2-only — a hire with no offer: the generic accept path advances Offer→Hired whenever no offer_review approval is pending, bypassing the extend-offer human gate — the demo produced '1 candidate hired this week' with no offer record, no candidate acceptance, no onboarding
expected: The product's own stated rule: 'Hired is set when the candidate accepts an offer, not by a manual move' — and /about's story: 'a person extends it, and the candidate accepts or declines through a secure link.'
got: The pipeline route enforces the rule for set_stage only (422 at app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:102-107) and reroutes accept to extendOffer only when approvalKind === 'offer_review' (:226-228). A plain accept POST on an Offer-stage entry with no pending approval falls to the generic advance (pipeline.ts:1332-1340) and lands Hired directly — no offer minted, no /api/offer/[token] acceptance, no onboarding handoff fired. Live: the sim did exactly this (via gsim-l2-101's advanceTo), and the board now announces '1 candidate hired this week — Vít Malý' for a candidate who was never offered anything. Beyond the sim, any API client or future automation can 'hire' the same way — the guard's own rationale (a hire with no offer record) is defeated on the accept path.

scope_note: Reachability 'med': the recruiter UI normally routes offers through offer_review so human clicks don't hit this; the exposed edge is programmatic/raced accepts — which is precisely what the product's own demo does, in front of the buyer it most needs to convince.
suggested_acceptance: The accept path mirrors the set_stage guard: Offer→Hired only through /api/offer/[token] acceptance (or an explicit, audited override); a unit test asserts a bare accept at Offer without an open offer is refused with the same 422 rationale.

title: NEW L2-only — the tamper-evident audit chain attributes the demo engine's API advances to 'human:recruiter' ('Recruiter accept from Accepted'), and the Analytics decision log renders HUMAN badges on rows whose own text says 'Auto-advanced'
expected: The audit surfaces — the product's 'Provable, not promised' pillar and Petra's 'what happened and to whom' criterion — record WHO acted truthfully: human actions as human, programmatic actions as automated.
got: Live, in the sealed 'Decision records (sealed)' list: nine records for this run's cohort ('#5..#13 · advanced human:recruiter · Recruiter accept from Accepted · m-cand-*-jd-dhbye8rf · 2026-07-02 14:22') — advances performed entirely by the sim engine via API, with no human present. In the decision log below it, the same actions render with a HUMAN badge next to the text 'Auto-advanced · <name> · Accepted → Screened' — the badge and the row text contradict each other on the same line. Code: the pipeline route seals EVERY accept/reject as actor 'human:recruiter' (app/api/pipeline/[id]/route.ts:249-259); actOnPipelineEntry records auto_* kinds only when passed actor:'system' (pipeline.ts:1292), which the route never passes; the sim posts plain accepts (SimulationProvider.tsx:247-252). The sim's one honest attribution — approvedBy 'Guided demo (auto-approved)' on the screen wave (SimulationProvider.tsx:484) — exists in the payload but never surfaced in any captured audit view.

shots/l2-helena-14-sim-phase-4screen-b.aria.txt:437-472 (decision log rows: HUMAN badge + 'Auto-advanced · …' text, 5s ago)

scope_note: In a real workspace a recruiter's click IS human — the misattribution is specific to programmatic callers (the sim today; any future automation via this route tomorrow). For a bank buyer evaluating an Art.22 dossier product, the audit misstating the actor is the sharpest possible own-goal; for Petra it breaks the exact log she cites to managers. suggested_acceptance: Programmatic/sim callers seal with an automation actor (e.g. 'auto:sim' / 'system'), the route accepts an actor hint only from trusted internal callers, and the decision-log badge derives from the same actor field as the row text — asserted by a test that a sim run yields zero 'human:recruiter' seals.
